textbookText: b. Trichocyst: Trichocysts are small, peculiar, rod-like or oval shaped organelles found in ectoplasm beneath the pellicle alternating with basal bodies. They lie right angle to the body surface and open by small pores on the ridges of hexagonal areas of pellicle. Each trichocyst consists of an elongated shaft and a terminal pointed tip, called spike covered by a cap like structure. Trichocyst is filled with a refractive dense fluid having a swelling substance. Discharge of trichocyst is triggered by external stimuli such as touch, chemical, temperature, electric current etc. Trichocysts are discharged as long, sticky threads in response to stimuli. At the moment of stimulation, the ectoplasm quickly contracts, separating the cap and spike of trichocyst. Consequently, water enters the sac of trichocyst and substance in the sac swells by absorbing water to form a filamentous spike for discharging out. A discharged trichocyst has an opaque spike like the inverted nail with a cap, attached to a long striated shaft. Shaft can’t be seen in undischarged trichocyst. Function: Trichocysts help to attach on solid object or substratum. They also help in offence and defence in some ciliates.

c. Nucleus: Paramecium caudatum possess two types of nuclei and this is called nuclear dimorphism. Larger, bean shaped nucleus is called macronucleus or meganucleus. Its function is to regulate the metabolic activities of its cell. It is also called somatic or vegetative nucleus. Similarly, the small and spherical shaped nucleus lying close or at the concavity of macronucleus is called micronucleus. Micronucleus controls the reproductive activity of Paramecium and so it is also called generative nucleus.
Questions to think? What will happen to Paramecium when micronucleus is removed from its cell body?

d. Contractile vacuole: Unlike Amoeba, there are two large liquid filled contractile vacuoles in Paramecium, each fixed at the anterior and posterior position closer to aboral surface in endoplasm. Contractile vacuoles open outside through permanent pore in pellicle on aboral surface. Sometimes, they may disappear temporarily. Each contractile vacuole is surrounded by about six to ten long, narrow tubular structures called radiating canals or radial canals. The radial canals communicate with the interior part of body from where they take up excess water and pour into the central vacuole. When the vacuole becomes fully turgid then it contracts and discharges its content through permanent pore in the pellicle. Posterior contractile vacuole contracts more frequently than the anterior contractile vacuole. Since, more water enters this vacuole as it is nearer to the cytopharynx. Function of contractile vacuole is osmoregulation i.e. maintaining water and salt in the body.

e. Food vacuole: Food vacuoles are also called gastrioles which are roughly spherical, non-contractile structures with variable numbers and size. They are found embedded in endoplasm. Food vacuoles contain ingested food particles such as bacteria, small amount of fluid along with digestive enzymes bounded by a thin membrane. They are seen, moving with the streaming cytoplasm (cyclosis) in the clockwise direction throughout the body. During the course of movement, food particles are digested, absorbed and assimilated.

f. Oral groove: Oral groove is a large oblique depression on the ventro-lateral side of the body, making the body of Paramecium asymmetrical shaped. Oral groove posteriorly lead s into a short conical funnel shaped depression called vestibule. Vestibule leads posteriorly into cytopharynx through a fixed oval shaped opening called cytostome (cell mouth). Cytopharynx runs obliquely downward and form new food vacuole at its proximal end. Several rows of cilia are found lining the oral apparatus and beating action of these cilia help in collecting and passing down food particles. The food particles are finally trapped in food vacuole.

g. Cytopyge (cell anus): At the time of egestion, a minute opening on the pellicle on ventral surface is visible, just behind the cytostome called cytopyge. Cytopyge is also called anal spot or cytoproct. This is used for expelling out undigested food particles.

Reproduction Reproduction is the life process in which living beings produce offspring of their own kind for the continuation of their generation. In Paramecium, asexual reproduction takes place by transverse binary fission and sexual reproduction takes place by various methods such as conjugation, endomixis, autogamy etc.
